Container.Name: Speech-To-Speech-CPU
Container.ExtraSearchTerms: voice stt tts whisper realtime websocket conduit openai speech to speech assistant microphone transcription kokoro cpu
Container.Overview: Speech-To-Speech-CPU runs Hugging Face's open-source realtime voice-agent pipeline (Apache-2.0, 13k+ stars): voice activity detection, speech-to-text (faster-whisper), any OpenAI-compatible LLM as the brain, and Kokoro text-to-speech — served as one OpenAI Realtime WebSocket server. Point any Realtime-API client at it instead of OpenAI's cloud: Conduit's "local listening" (speech server), OpenAI Agents SDK clients, LiveKit, or its own browser demo. This template runs a CPU image built and published by Aurial (upstream ships CUDA-only and no registry image), so it needs no GPU and can run alongside GPU inference servers. It has no web page of its own: it is a backend that apps connect to. Configure the three LLM fields below to point at an existing OpenAI-compatible server (Strata, Radiance, Ollama, LM Studio, …); the key is stored masked, never on the command line. One voice session at a time by default; first start downloads the speech models (a few GB) into the cache folder, then it is warm and CPU-light.
Container.Requires: An OpenAI-compatible LLM server reachable over your network (Strata, Radiance, Ollama, etc.) — its URL and key go in the LLM fields below. The pipeline cannot start without it (it warms up the backend before opening the port). First start downloads STT/TTS models into the cache folder: allow 1–2 minutes before the port opens. Nothing else: pure CPU, no GPU flags, no driver plugin.

Config.Name: Realtime port
Config.Description: OpenAI Realtime WebSocket endpoint: ws://SERVER:8765/v1/realtime (this is what Conduit's speech server / Realtime clients connect to). Only needs to be reachable from your LAN/tailnet — do not expose it to the internet.

Config.Name: Models & cache folder
Config.Description: Holds the downloaded speech models (faster-whisper + Kokoro voices, a few GB) and pip/HF caches. Keep it on a fast pool if you have one; without a persistent folder the models re-download on every recreate.

Config.Name: LLM server URL
Config.Description: Base URL (with /v1) of your OpenAI-compatible LLM server that will act as the brain — e.g. http://192.168.150.32:8180/v1 for Strata or Radiance on this machine. REQUIRED: the pipeline warms this backend up before opening the realtime port.

Config.Name: LLM API key
Config.Description: API key for the LLM server above (stored masked). Leave empty if your server has no auth. An empty/wrong key here shows up as a 401 in the container log at startup.

Config.Name: Model name
Config.Description: The exact model name the LLM server serves (what GET /v1/models reports), e.g. qwen3.8-flash-next-q4. Leave empty to use the server default.

Config.Name: STT engine
Config.Description: Speech-to-text backend. faster-whisper is the tested CPU default; whisper (openai) also works. Run 'speech-to-speech serve -h' in a console for the full list.

Config.Name: TTS engine
Config.Description: Text-to-speech backend. Kokoro is the tested CPU default (fast, natural). Only used when a client asks the server to speak — Conduit listen-only mode ignores it.

Config.Name: Compute device
Config.Description: Leave cpu. The image ships CPU torch wheels; AMD GPUs are not supported by this pipeline and your GPU is better left to the LLM server.
